summary: Vinhos is a dense, multi-layered economic game where you juggle vineyard planting, wine production, quality upgrades, trade fairs, and contracts across six harvest years, with almost every turn forcing tight trade-offs between several viable strategies. It plays like a spreadsheet come to life — deeply satisfying once the engine clicks, but demanding heavy upfront study of interlocking subsystems.
praised: Rich, interlocking decision space where every action has ripple effects
Strong thematic integration of wine-making stages into mechanics
High replayability from variable player powers, contracts, and events
Satisfying sense of building and optimizing an efficient engine
criticised: Steep learning curve and rules overhead, especially for a first play
Dense iconography and a lot of fiddly bookkeeping
Significant analysis paralysis, especially with more players
Can feel more like a solitaire optimization puzzle than an interactive game

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking, area majority at the trade fair, and competing for limited contracts

scoring.why: final score combines wine quality/exports, contracts fulfilled, vineyard and building investments, and end-game bonuses, so success comes from balancing several economic engines rather than one dominant path
